featured_reviews.name: Aniket Salvi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Joined Cult Gym at Wadala due to proximity where I stay. The gym equipment are good with variety however gym requires following improvements:

1. Availability and engagement of General Trainer - This gym is solely focused on P. T. i.e., Personal Training and at any given time except in morning there is no general trainer on floor to help regular members and instilling gym etiquettes in some unruly and miscreant members which isn’t happening at all. I have gone to Cult gym Prabhadevi where there’s always a general trainer on floor who helps if asked or does proactively and also corrects the persons not following gym etiquettes properly.

2. Management - Management team of the gym is very ineffective and not that strong. We all work for money but a Gym is a holy place for many peoples and it should be handled like a School or College wherein there should be strict discipline and code of conduct which isn’t thing taken seriously in the gym. Members come here to Socialize, hog machines, not keeping dumbbells' / weights / rods in designated place after use, no social sense of presence of other peoples around, wearing headphones and talking loudly, banging weights, etc. I have been to local gyms where though machinery is average and not that high profile, but at least management is strong enough to instill discipline in members.

3. Timings - Gym is operational till 10:30, however most of the good and high profile gyms in our area are open till 11:00 p.m. Gym can be kept open till 11:00 p.m. very effectively without any hesitation.

4. Availability of Steam - Steam is available only on Wednesday’s and Saturday’s which was informed when joined. However sometimes steam is abruptly closed or not available on designated days without any prior notice and just putting up a piece of paper as government circular on notice board on same day.

5. Gym closed on public holidays and Sundays - Gym is closed on many of the public holidays on top of being closed on Sundays. Most of the gyms in Mumbai are either open full day on Sundays or at least for half day till noon. I agree that holidays are part and parcel of every job, but being a cult gym other cult gyms around our areas are open on public holidays and Sundays too.

Conclusion:
I have just joined this gym due to availability of good machinery, fame of Cult and proximity near my residence, however after paying a good hefty yearly fees, overall ambience, vibes and mood is like any other local AC gym in any good area. So think before joining gym just based on exterior appearance and name.

featured_reviews.review_text:
The gym overall has a great look and feel and genuinely gives off a strong community vibe, which was one of the main reasons I decided to visit. Unfortunately, the experience at the reception completely ruined that first impression.

I had booked a free trial on May 15th (Friday) and was expecting a callback as mentioned in the instructions. Due to personal commitments, I could only finally visit on May 20th regarding(Tuesday), despite never receiving any call for the trial.

What happened at the reception was honestly disappointing and insulting. Initially, the One of the staff outright denied that any free trial even exist now and instead pushed for a paid day pass for 400Rs. Only later did the other  receptionist came and acknowledged that a free trial is offered. While speaking to her superior over the call, she openly said things like “The opposite side gym is closed today because of XYZ reason, should we  give the free trial?” — and this entire conversation happened right in front of "Another Customer". Superior on the call was kind of enough to offer free trial which I denied taking due to such negative experience.

Instead of handling the situation professionally and simply asking basic questions like *when the trial was booked* or checking the details properly, I was subjected to completely unnecessary and irrelevant questioning. The entire interaction made me feel as though I was doing something wrong or trying to scam the gym just for asking about a trial that was officially offered and booked beforehand.

A free trial is meant to attract potential members and create a welcoming first impression — not make people feel embarrassed, judged, or publicly questioned. The receptionist’s tone and handling of the situation were extremely unprofessional and lacked even basic courtesy or customer respect.

Honestly, if this is how potential customers are treated before even joining, it raises serious concerns about the gym’s overall customer experience when expanding despite the otherwise positive atmosphere inside.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Five Gardens area in Matunga is part of the famous Dadar-Parsi colony. This area was specially established for the upper class Parsis in the very early 19th century by the efforts of Mancherji Edalji Joshi, a renowned Parsi patron. The British however built it under the scheme of Bombay City Improvement Plan for the localities of Dadar, Matunga, Wadala, Sion in 1899-1900. So this is the first planned area of the city with spaces allocated for residences, green space, schools and colleges with proximity to transport infrastructure
The purpose was to de-congest the city after the Bombay Bubonic Plague Epidemic which broke in the September of 1896. According to the plan they wanted to house about 60,000 people in Sion and about 85,000 in Dadar & Matunga. Now there is as much people in every square kilometer of this area
So back to the garden itself. These are exactly five gardens just like shown in the map above. Getting here is quite simple. This is at a walking distance from King’s Circle and if you take the train get down at either Matunga or King’s Circle Railway Station and then take the taxi.
The garden itself is like any other Government infrastructure waiting to fall apart.

I joined AISW one year ago.

On my very first day, I met a trainer who was calm, composed, and deeply confident in what he knew. He understood exactly what I needed, even before I could explain it properly myself. I signed up with him as my personal trainer immediately.

That trainer was Veeraj Sir.

Before we even started training seriously, he tested my body strength, stamina, mobility, and muscle capacity. There was never any rush. His philosophy was simple: progress slowly, but correctly. Every workout had purpose. Warm-ups and stretches were just as important to him as lifting weights.

And somehow, through an entire year of training, I never dealt with the kind of post-workout pain or injuries people usually talk about.

When I joined, I was overweight. Honestly, I still am… just a few kilos less now 😄
But I’ve already lost 15 kgs.

Today, I can box squat 70 kgs without pain. My chest, biceps, core, stamina, and overall strength are in a much better place.

But the biggest transformation was not physical.

My daily medicines reduced from 7 to just 2.
My blood pressure medicines disappeared.
No diabetes medication anymore.
Even my doctor asked me to stop taking multivitamins.

I feel energetic again.
I’m playing the best cricket of my life.
And most importantly…
I ended my long, exhausting relationship with back pain.

That alone changed my quality of life.

Veeraj Sir didn’t just help me lose weight. He helped me regain confidence in my own body again.

One year later, I can genuinely say that one of the things that impressed me most about him is his deep understanding of the science of the human body. The way he explains muscle function, recovery, movement, posture, and overall physiology makes you realize that his training is not random — every exercise has a scientific reason behind it. He understands how the body works and adapts, and that knowledge reflects in the safe, effective, and sustainable progress his clients make.

Now I’m looking forward to another year under his guidance. This next year feels less about fitness and more about transformation.

And honestly, the biggest compliment I can give him is this:
I’m already trying to convince my son to train under him during his school vacations ❤️

Thank you, Veeraj Sir.
